project.name: CampusSecure
project.description: CampusSecure is a fictional university student portal for an authorized, isolated information security laboratory. Its Flask and SQLite application demonstrates server-side ownership, role, and field authorization through controlled API scenarios.

tour.title: Project and Lab Overview
tour.description: Start with the project guide and specification to see why this fictional university portal exists and what its student, administrator, and laboratory workflows cover. They establish the isolated teaching setting, the Flask and SQLite architecture, and the security boundaries that later stops explain in code.

tour.title: Runtime and Application Factory
tour.description: Following the setup in Step 1, run.py starts the local server and validates an explicitly selected private interface when a wider bind is requested. The Flask factory chooses the lab mode at startup, loads the user, checks POST CSRF tokens, registers blueprints, and handles errors; requirements.txt records the runtime Flask dependency.

tour.title: SQLite and Fictional Fixtures
tour.description: The factory's central dependency is app/db.py, which owns the SQLite schema, request-scoped connection, and teardown behavior. Its repeatable fictional fixtures support the seed command, while the reset command restores a known starting state for each lab comparison.

tour.title: Sessions and HTML Access
tour.description: With persistent accounts in place, app/auth.py handles sign-in and sign-out and provides the decorator used to require authentication or a role on HTML views. The login template submits credentials with a CSRF token, linking the browser form to the factory's POST protection from Step 2.

tour.title: Student Portal Workflows
tour.description: Building on the session and database rules, student routes show a dashboard, allow contact edits, and list or display requests filtered to the signed-in student. The dashboard and request templates show how those server-side ownership checks become student-facing pages and statuses.

tour.title: Administrator Portal Workflows
tour.description: The administrator blueprint uses the same authentication and SQLite foundation to summarize activity, review academic requests, and manage announcements. Its request-detail and announcement templates expose the review and editing forms, with CSRF tokens on state-changing actions.

tour.title: JSON Request Ownership
tour.description: After the HTML workflows, app/api.py introduces the JSON request-read endpoint used for a controlled ownership comparison. app/lab_policy.py centralizes the mode-dependent authorization decision, so the same endpoint can demonstrate why a request's owner must be checked on the server.

tour.title: JSON Announcement Role
tour.description: The next API scenario uses announcement creation to test whether the caller has the administrator role already required in the HTML workflow. The route validates input, while the policy module makes the secure and vulnerable authorization outcomes comparable without changing the route or schema.

tour.title: JSON Profile Field Control
tour.description: The final JSON scenario updates a profile and asks which fields the server allows a student to change. Read the API validation beside the mode-dependent policy to connect this field authorization decision to the contact-only edit flow from Step 5.

tour.title: Shared Portal Frontend
tour.description: After tracing the server decisions, the shared Jinja shell explains how navigation, assets, and page content are assembled for both roles. The status macro, portal stylesheet, and browser script add consistent badges, responsive layouts, form feedback, confirmations, and request-table filtering.

tour.title: Regression and Mode Tests
tour.description: The tests now verify the account, role, ownership, CSRF, fixture, and page behavior seen in earlier steps against isolated SQLite databases. Dedicated mode tests compare the three JSON decisions and check reset and host-binding behavior, making the teaching scenarios repeatable.

tour.title: Architecture and Lab Evidence
tour.description: The architecture document maps the blueprints, tables, templates, and isolated deployment boundary covered so far. The lab guide gives the manual Ubuntu, Kali, and Burp procedure, while the security report records the three controlled findings, expected controls, and evidence still to collect.

tour.title: Standalone Web Presentation
tour.description: The offline web deck turns the architecture and lab evidence from Step 12 into seven slides with scenario comparisons and screenshot slots. Its README explains presentation controls, while the stylesheet and script provide responsive staging, navigation, scenario switching, and local screenshot loading.

tour.title: Editable Presentation Deliverable
tour.description: The presentation outline frames the same seven-slide story for a university audience, and the builder creates and validates an editable PowerPoint deck. Read the finished deck with its speaker notes to see how the lab architecture, three authorization scenarios, remediation, and results are communicated outside the running portal.
